dispatch: Lane zero occupies the low slices. dispatch_i is the externally accepted oldest prefix, shared atomically with backend allocation, not an offer. The caller uses dispatch_ready_o to reserve pre-cycle credits before accepting the whole selected prefix; no issue-credit bypass, enqueue-to-issue bypass or internal partial acceptance. Incoming source readiness is authoritative and must already include backend accepted-WB and intra-bundle RAW handling. Unused sources use p0. Payload is an opaque 64-bit execution token (initially instruction and PC); destination and full ROB identity are retained separately. Commit-only operations bypass this queue and require a future head controller.
selection: Sparse IQ storage, oldest first by five-bit modulo-32 distance from the current ROB head. Every resident identity must remain live in the common at-most-32-entry ROB window, with one instruction per ROB slot. The full eight-bit generation is forwarded unchanged but does not define age. Port zero selects its oldest ready eligible instruction first; port one selects its oldest ready eligible unchosen instruction. Eligibility 01 is branch/ALU0, 10 is AGU/ALU1, 11 is either ALU port. 00 is illegal. This preserves the A1 policy; maximum matching and cross-port oldest issue ordering are not promised.
issue: issue_o is a ready-qualified launch pulse, not a held valid offer. port_ready_i must reflect execution holding-register and downstream resource availability independent of the selected payload. A pulse consumes the entry at the edge; no pulse means no consumption. Operands use read_address_o on the corresponding two PRF read ports. Wakeup and PRF data bypass consume exactly the same accepted backend writeback transaction. Queue operands contain tags, not values.
wakeup: Two physical destination broadcasts qualified by wb_accept_i, which must come from backend_two_wide.wb_accept_o after generation, ownership, fault and recovery checks. Raw producer offers are forbidden. A resident match permits same-cycle selection and latches readiness if the port is stalled. p0 is always ready. The queue does not independently validate producer generations or suppress a falsely accepted stale writeback. Incoming dispatch readiness must already incorporate same-cycle accepted WB; enqueue does not independently reapply broadcasts.
recovery: Reset and flush clear validity and suppress dispatch/issue. flush_i includes accepted traps and whole-window replay. recover_i denotes the single already-validated winning branch recovery; head_slot_i and recover_slot_i refer to the pre-cycle ROB window. It suppresses all dispatch and issue for that cycle and kills entries strictly younger than the branch using wrap-safe distance, retaining the branch and older entries. Accepted surviving WB may latch readiness during branch recovery. Upstream validates the recovery identity, arbitrates oldest recovery, and filters killed WB. Reset, flush, branch recovery and identity-drain must be coordinated across backend, IQ and every producer; an empty IQ alone does not acknowledge global quiescence.
scope: Standalone full-size IQ with synthetic live ROB, dispatch, accepted writeback and execution readiness. No connected backend/IQ integration, instruction execution, memory launch, CSR/MMIO serialization, frontend, integrated formal proof or complete OOO processor acceptance. Generic synthesis does not close the A1 physical issue/read/execute timing gate.
